lead: Cases del Governador, squares with fountains and a festa major in May.
text: It was farmland in the municipality of Sant Martí de Provençals, annexed by Barcelona in 1897, and remained almost uninhabited until the 20th century; its development began in the 1950s. Its name comes from Carrer de Navas de Tolosa, one of its axes, where the metro station of the same name stands, and from 1978 its residents campaigned for an identity of their own, which was officially recognised in 2006.

Plaça de Fernando Reyes, with the church of Sant Joan Bosco, is its centre, and Plaça d'Islàndia has a cascading fountain. The Cases del Governador are 406 low-rise houses surrounded by landscaped spaces, inspired by the garden-city model. At 4,029 €/m², it has the highest sale price in Sant Andreu, and it holds its festa major every May.
housing: Blocks of flats and the Cases del Governador, low-rise with communal gardens.
